correctness.rationale: The additive-increment period set T={u:g(x+u)-g(x)=g(u) for all x} is an F_p-vector subspace; the additive index is q/|T| by linear extension from T. Cyclotomic homogeneity g(hx)=h^r g(x) for h in H=(F_q*)^ell makes T invariant under H. For ell|q-1 and ell<=p, ell<=p-1, so |H|>p^(n-1) if n>=2; a nonzero T must contain Hu and hence all F_q. If T=F_q, g is linearized with degree<=p^(n-1), and agreement with a monomial on >p^(n-1) elements of H forces exactly one Frobenius term; n=1 is immediate. For odd p, f(x)=x+c x^p, norm(c)!=1, is an invertible F_p-linear non-Frobenius map with ell exactly p+1. Independent F9 presentation enumeration ell=1,2 examined all 320 presentations and found only period dimensions 0 and 2, and tested the sharpness construction; finite check corroborates the all-prime argument.

value.rationale: Sharp low-multiplicative-index rigidity for additive structure is an exact uniform algebraic boundary of a natural finite-field invariant. Excluding every intermediate additive index and exhibiting a sharp p+1 permutation counterexample clarifies how cyclotomic homogeneity constrains additive periods; it is substantially more informative than the known lower bound p.

final_claim: For f:F_(p^n)->F_(p^n) with g=f-f(0) zero-free away from 0 and cyclotomic multiplicative index ell<=p, either g(x)=a x^(p^j) with a nonzero and AddInd(f)=1 or AddInd(f)=p^n, with no intermediate additive index. For every odd prime p, the cutoff is sharp at ell=p+1 via a non-Frobenius linearized permutation on F_(p^2).
limitations: Assumes zero-free g on F_q* and defined ordinary cyclotomic index; cannot generalize to arbitrary functions.
Sharpness stated for all odd p, not automatically for p=2.
The 2022 original additive-index foundation was bibliographically identified but the full text was not read; originality retains explicit priority risk.
